task.description: Validate test/specs/REQ-151.md and test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs against every REQ-151 acceptance criterion, per WF-02 Step 3b's standard procedure: re-run the suite directly, confirm no skips/TODOs/hardcoded secrets, confirm fixture/test independence, and -- because this is a newly-created module whose pre-fix state is 'the module did not exist' rather than a behavioral regression -- apply at least one real mutant to lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex, confirm it isolates a real test failure, then revert and re-verify clean.
acceptance_criteria: At least one runnable test targets each REQ-151 acceptance criterion -- no @tag :skip without a passing counterpart
No 'TODO: implement test' left in spec or test file
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test pollution / shared hardcoded state
Tests are self-sufficient -- don't depend on other tests running first
No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in test files
mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs passes with real output quoted
A real mutant applied to sandbox.ex is shown to isolate a genuine test failure, then reverted with a clean re-run confirmed

result.summary:
Read test/specs/REQ-151.md, test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs, lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex, and docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-151 entry (7 acceptance criteria, lines 78-85) directly.

Coverage: all 7 REQ-151 acceptance criteria map to a runnable test per the spec's own AC-to-test-case table: AC1 (single call site) -> section 1's System.cmd grep assertion; AC2 (14 named paths nil-or-raise) -> section 2's 14 per-path tests plus section 4's 4 debug-internals tests; AC3 (custom :sandboxed list trap guard / REQ-152 named) -> section 3's two trap-guard tests plus section 7's REQ-152-named moduledoc test; AC4 (LUA-03 restatement, 3 reasons) -> section 7's three moduledoc assertions (loadstring/5.1, jit/ffi/bit vacuity, SBX-1); AC5 (LUA-04 restatement, structural) -> section 7's bytecode/structurally assertion; AC6 (deny-set explicit with per-entry reason, coroutine decision explicit) -> section 5's coroutine-is-nil test plus source-level review of @sandbox_deny_set (28 entries in sandbox.ex, each carrying a distinct reason string) plus section 7's coroutine-decision moduledoc test; AC7 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass) -> verified directly below (TEST-RUNNER's formal Step 4 responsibility per the spec's own note, but re-run here for this gate).

Hygiene checks: grep for 'TODO' and '@tag :skip' across both files returned zero hits. grep for password/secret/postgres:///api_key returned zero hits (no hardcoded secrets). All 30 tests build their Lua.t() inline per-test via Sandbox.new/0 or new/1 -- no shared setup/fixture state, no test depends on another's prior execution, no database or HTTP touched anywhere in the file (confirmed by reading the moduledoc's own claim and the test bodies), so async: true is safe and tests are self-sufficient.

Re-ran the suite directly: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs` -> 'Result: 30 passed', 0 failures.

Mutant-isolation check (required because this module is newly created -- the pre-fix state is 'Letflow.Engine.Lua.Sandbox did not exist', so a pre-fix-failure confirmation alone would prove nothing about whether these tests discriminate a correct implementation from a wrong one). Applied one real mutant directly to the shipped source: removed the `{[:os, :exit], "Installed (os_exit/2). Real denial..."}` entry from `@sandbox_deny_set` in lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex (a real, non-vacuous denial per the source's own comments, not one of the vacuous/no-op entries). Re-ran the suite: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs` -> 'Result: 29/30 passed, Failed: 1 test' -- exactly the 'os.exit raises when called' test failed, with actual output 'Wrong message for Lua.RuntimeException, expected: ~r/sandboxed/, actual: "Lua runtime error: os.exit is not supported in embedded mode (at <eval>:1)"' (the library's own built-in guard fires instead of this module's sandboxing, so the regex on the '<name> is sandboxed' message no longer matches). This isolates a genuine, single-test failure caused specifically by the mutant, proving the test discriminates the correct deny-set from a narrowed one. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex`; confirmed via `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` (empty output, clean) and a clean re-run: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs` -> 'Result: 30 passed', 0 failures.

No gaps found against any acceptance criterion. No rewrite of TEST-DESIGNER's tests was needed.
